prompt: Each backend server is slow 1% of the time. A search request fans out to 100 of them and waits for all.
why: 1 − 0.99¹⁰⁰ ≈ 63% of requests hit at least one slow server. The tail becomes typical.
trap: Average latency looks fine; the fan-out exposes the tail.

prompt: To cut p99, a client sends a second copy of a request to another replica if the first hasn't answered within the p95 time.
why: Hedged requests trim the tail for a few percent extra load.
trap: Not a retry storm: the copy is sent only for the slowest few percent.

prompt: The dashboard shows average latency of 80 ms, yet users complain the app often feels slow. Pages make about 20 backend calls each.
why: With 20 calls per page, most pages hit some call's p95 or p99. Watch percentiles, not averages.
trap: Averages hide the slow calls that define the user's experience.

prompt: A dashboard query merges results from 40 shards. One shard with an overloaded disk makes every dashboard slow.
why: When you wait for all parts, the slowest part sets the response time.
trap: The overloaded disk is a knee problem on one shard; the fan-out is why everyone feels it.
